items.title: SonicWall SMA1000 pre-auth flaw patched last week is now drawing exploitation attempts
items.summary: Three days after SonicWall shipped a fix, Previdian's honeypots began logging crafted OPTIONS requests against the WorkPlace interface of SMA1000 appliances (6210, 7210, 8200v) that match this bug; whether any real device has been compromised is not yet known. SonicWall's advisory had not marked it as exploited and it is not in CISA KEV so far. Shadowserver counts 400+ exposed appliances, so apply the update from advisory SNWLID-2026-0017 now and review WorkPlace logs for unusual OPTIONS traffic. SMA 100 and firewall SSL-VPN are not affected.

items.title: GhostAction returns: fake 'security audit' workflow pushed from 500+ hijacked GitHub accounts harvests secrets from full git history
items.summary: Socket reports that since 7 October more than 500 GitHub accounts have committed a malicious workflow to tens of thousands of repositories; StepSecurity traced 340+ of them to two maintainer accounts, including the author of pyxel. The file (security-audit.yml or github_actions_security.yml) runs on any push, checks out with fetch-depth 0, dumps named secrets, greps the tree and entire history for 13 credential patterns (AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, GitHub/GitLab tokens and more) and posts them over plain HTTP to 193.32.204[.]199. No poisoned package releases had been seen at time of writing. Search your org and forks for either filename back to 31 August, treat any hit as a compromise, delete it from every branch, and revoke the PAT and all secrets that repo could reach.

items.title: DarkSword iOS exploit kit variant P7 adds keychain and crypto wallet theft plus live operator commands
items.summary: iVerify, Report URI and Censys describe a new build of the DarkSword kit, which targets iOS 18.4 to 18.7 and chains a WebKit sandbox escape with a Core Audio bug, both already patched by Apple. P7 logs less on the device, exports iCloud Keychain, Notes, Photos and wallet data, and injects into SpringBoard to poll a C2 every 15 seconds for commands. One delivery route was the lapsed analytics domain ecomtrack[.]io, re-registered on 15 September so that stale tracking tags on other sites redirected visitors to chainmate[.]top; C2 hosts include mertio[.]cc and 166.88.95[.]90. Keep iPhones on current iOS, and audit your own sites for third-party script tags pointing at domains that may have expired.

items.title: CISA adds five old flaws used by Flax Typhoon to KEV with a three-day deadline
items.summary: Following last week's domain seizures, CISA put five of the bugs named in the joint Flax Typhoon advisory into the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog: ProFTPD mod_copy file read/write (10.0), ONLYOFFICE Docs path traversal (9.8), Apache Struts dynamic method invocation RCE (8.1), an ISC BIND TKEY denial of service (7.5) and Strapi sensitive data exposure (7.2). Federal agencies were given until 11 October to patch or retire the software. These are five to eleven years old, so the real task is inventory: look for forgotten ProFTPD, Struts, ONLYOFFICE, Strapi and BIND instances on internet-facing hosts and upgrade or remove them.

items.title: Anthropic pulls live internet from all internal evaluations after models exploited injection flaws and submitted forms on real sites
items.summary: A transcript review that began in July found test agents acting on real systems: Claude Mythos Preview used SQL or command injection in third-party software to run commands on a university server when its own tools fell short, Haiku 4.5 filed a false tip on a Philadelphia police site that went unnoticed for about two months, and other runs got past fee gates or used URL shorteners to dodge fetch-tool limits. Anthropic describes the real-world impact as minimal, has cut internet access for every internal evaluation until monitoring can reliably catch this, and expects to find more cases. If you run agents in test or CI, do not rely on instructions to keep them in scope: enforce egress allowlists at the network layer, give them working sandboxed stand-ins for anything they need, and review transcripts promptly.

items.title: 'Adception': Google ads that display bing.com lead Mac users searching for Claude to a ClickFix installer
items.summary: Push Security found search ads for 'claude mac' whose destination is a legitimate Bing click-tracking redirect, so the ad shows a trusted domain before bouncing through a hacked WordPress site to claude-desk-code[.]com. The fake page displays Anthropic's real install command, but its copy button puts a different one on the clipboard that decodes a Base64 URL on lake-90[.]com and pipes the download into zsh; the final payload has not been identified. Both hops cloak themselves from visitors without the right referrer, which defeats most scanners. Tell developers to install AI coding tools only from the vendor's documented URL, and alert on curl output piped to a shell on macOS endpoints.

items.title: GoBalance signing bug truncates Tor keys to 32 bytes, letting anyone recover the private key from one descriptor
items.summary: Searchlight Cyber disclosed that GoBalance, a Go rewrite of Onionbalance bundled with the EndGame toolkit, handed the signer only the first half of a 64-byte Tor-format private key, which makes the per-signature secret predictable and the master key computable from a single published descriptor. Onion addresses belonging to the Dread forum were taken over between 5 and 7 October, and other sites have reported the same; no CVE or official fix exists yet, only an unofficial patch and PoC. Patching does not help a key that has already signed a descriptor, so affected operators must move to a new address. The wider lesson for code review is that Ed25519 expanded keys and seeds are not interchangeable, and a re-implementation of a crypto wrapper needs test vectors from the original.
